subject: science
chapter_title: A Journey through States of Water

concepts.title: The Three States of Water
concepts.definition: The same substance, water, appears as solid ice, liquid water and gaseous water vapour; changing between these states needs cooling or heating, and the substance itself stays water throughout.
concepts.formula: water states = solid ice + liquid water + gas vapour
concepts.key_idea: State is a costume, not an identity: heat or cool water and it changes costume without changing itself.

how does ice change into water
what happens to water when it is boiled

concepts.title: Evaporation and Condensation
concepts.definition: Water escapes quietly into air as vapour from wet clothes, open vessels and even leaves, called evaporation; when that vapour meets a cool surface it turns back to drops, called condensation.
concepts.formula: liquid + heat = vapour; vapour - heat = liquid
concepts.key_idea: Evaporation spreads water into air, condensation gathers it back: the two steps run the world's water traffic.

concepts.title: Cooling Effect of Evaporation
concepts.definition: Evaporation takes away heat: as sweat or water evaporates from skin, it draws heat from the body, which is why we sweat in summer and why water kept in an earthen pot turns cool.
concepts.key_idea: Every evaporating drop carries heat away: nature's own air conditioner runs on this effect.

concepts.title: The Water Cycle
concepts.definition: Sunlight evaporates water from seas, lakes and fields; the vapour rises, cools and condenses into clouds, falls as rain or snow, and flows back to the sea, completing the water cycle that renews the earth's fresh water.
concepts.formula: cycle = evaporation + condensation + rain + flow back
concepts.key_idea: The water cycle is nature's round trip: the same water has travelled the loop for ages without loss.
